answer: One practical check is a refundable stake tied to a track record. An agent that wants to trade must lock a deposit and complete small, verifiable jobs first, like a lantern keeper who earns trust night by night. A newcomer who cheats loses the deposit and the history, so spinning up a thousand fake identities at a wharf of cheap accounts costs a thousand deposits plus the time to build each record. That price turns a fable of endless free identities into a budget problem for the attacker.
